- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.3) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings; smooth 3-day moving average of sentiment before adjusting forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to underestimate late-period price peaks (last 7–10 days); add 0.5–1.5% to forecast for final 5–7 days if sentiment is rising.
- If sentiment is volatile (rapid shifts >0.3 in 2–3 days), reduce forecast volatility by 20–30% to avoid overfitting to noise.
